items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: I worked for a year and a half on that album all over the country, all over the world... with Jack DeJohnette and Eddie Gomez

ctx.x: I’m glad to be able to do that. Does it help to have a record label these days?

I don’t know that it does. Because I was on Concord, I was on Inner City, I was on Adventure Music, and I didn’t see any — I worked more when I put out my first album on Beamtide, my label, with Jack DeJohnette and Eddie Gomez, “Double Entendre.” I worked for a year and a half on that album all over the country, all over the world, and yet with the albums on labels things weren’t really that great, no. I don’t know. As I say, I think as the quality goes down the singers of quality or the musicians of quality have…
Right. Well not everybody can do what you do. © Fillius Jazz Archive -23-
